0e5a513a4dd76f23c9f6efefd84c2eee3da1aec8: Formigal offers 143 km of well-marked runs: a mid-sized ski area, ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 21 lifts are generally enough to handle the flow in high season. Formigal's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for getting children started on skiing. Formigal's altitude (1510 m at the bottom, 2265 m at the top) helps it keep a decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Formigal is clearly on the expensive side: a day lift pass at 62€, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Formigal keeps its promises. A Pyrenean resort that will suit most types of skier without disappointing.

0ec1076015557cecb5dc9f0a5e949503524a2927: A resort on a human scale, Grüsch Danusa focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 31 km of runs are perfect for a 3–4 day stay, especially with family or for skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Grüsch Danusa's family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Grüsch Danusa's modest altitude — starting at 600 m, topping out at 1800 m — makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking the snow reports before setting off is strongly recommended. A stay in Grüsch Danusa is clearly on the expensive side: 64€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you go. In short: Grüsch Danusa doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

0ef15d797f5a159fa1b1af42b86efa3c415897d6: Tignes and Val d'Isère, joined since 1965 by the Col de Fresse, form a 300 km ski area, one of the largest and highest in the Alps. It is a ski area for purists: high altitude from bottom to top, the Grande Motte glacier skiable up to 3456 m, and snow almost guaranteed from October to May. The two resorts complement each other more than they resemble one another: Val d'Isère has the charm of a genuine Savoyard village and a reputation as a chic resort, while Tignes embraces its 1960s architecture and its sporty atmosphere. Off-piste here is among the most renowned in Europe.
